statusDetail: Complete atomic coverage of all 58 catalog checks across six representative public paths. Authenticated gameplay, payment, account management, and destructive account actions were intentionally not covered because they require credentials or side effects.

page.notes: Public multilingual board-game platform. Coverage includes landing, catalogue, detail, editorial, signup, and error templates. Authenticated live gameplay, premium checkout, account settings, and full game sessions were not covered because they require an account and would create side effects.

paths.description: Public landing and primary call-to-action; represents marketing entry, preference handling, discovery, metadata, and initial load.
Public game catalogue/listing; represents dense reusable cards, filtering, carousels, mobile layout, performance, and repeated interaction.
Representative game detail/entity and the Learn/Play decision point.
Primary public account-creation flow and input-assistance/error-handling surface.
Representative HTTP/navigation failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Screenshot comparison under emulated dark preference shows the same light #f7f7f7 landing surface; CSS only switches when an html.dark class is set, so the system preference does not select dark mode.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance dark-mode: address the measured divergence for respects color scheme and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-reduced-motion: non-essential animations and auto-advance are reduced or removed when the user asks for less motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched prefers-reduced-motion: reduce but still found infinite 1.75s fa-blink animations and many non-zero transitions.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance accessibility: address the measured divergence for respects reduced motion and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: CSS/DOM probe found no view-transition rules and route changes use full, abrupt document swaps across the representative navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance cross-document-transitions: address the measured divergence for view transitions and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Gesture-driven interactions and entry/exit motion feel native (declarative overscroll/scroll-snap, physics-based easing, animating to intrinsic sizes, pull/swipe gestures) rather than fighting the platform with custom pointer handlers.
findings.evidence: The game listing exposes horizontally paged carousels, but CSS inspection found no scroll-snap or overscroll declarations; movement is handled by custom arrow controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance carousel-slide-effects: address the measured divergence for physical gestures and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: Screenshots and CSS show static fixed navigation without a scroll-progress or scroll-state response despite long pages of 5,877 to 9,259 CSS px.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance scroll-progress-indicator: address the measured divergence for scroll state aware chrome and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Tooltips, popovers and menus use CSS anchor positioning (with fallback positions) so they stay attached and reposition correctly rather than being manually positioned.
findings.evidence: Menus and panels are implemented with fixed/absolute positioning in the captured CSS; no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try declarations were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance position-aware-tooltips: address the measured divergence for anchored positioning and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements while signup and menu overlays are custom containers, so modal/disclosure semantics and platform light-dismiss are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance declarative-dialog-popover-control: address the measured divergence for semantic dismissible primitives and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The layout adapts at viewport breakpoints, but live CSS inspection found no @container/container-type rules for reused game cards and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance size-aware-styling: address the measured divergence for component level responsiveness and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: Focus probes retain a native outline, but Lighthouse target-size audits fail and the live probe found many links only 14 to 15px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance accessibility: address the measured divergence for input modality aware and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 28.5s/TBT 600ms, gamelist LCP 28.4s/CLS 0.159, and signup LCP 23.2s/CLS 0.158.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance performance: address the measured divergence for good core web vitals and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout observers measured CLS 0.287 on home and 0.299 on gamelist; all 17 inspected images lacked width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance visually-stable-font-fallbacks: address the measured divergence for visual stability and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: The main thread is not blocked by long tasks or heavy scripting; work is deferred, chunked, prioritised, or moved off-thread.
findings.evidence: Trace recorded three long tasks and 59.66ms TBT under a fast local run; throttled Lighthouse measured 600 to 710ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance break-up-long-tasks: address the measured divergence for efficient main thread and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 4.99MB transferred, including three parser-blocking stylesheets and three classic parser-inserted scripts without async/defer/module confirmed by DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance optimize-script-priority: address the measured divergence for efficient resource delivery and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: The landing page ships 3.88MB of JavaScript; sveltec alone is 2.12MB and legacy Dojo plus analytics bundles load before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance identify-heavy-scripts: address the measured divergence for trim unused and duplicate code and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image-alt, link-name, label-content-name-mismatch, and signup form-label audits; the listing probe shows numerous image-only game links with no accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance accessibility: address the measured divergence for names roles labels and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audit fails on all three tested templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance accessibility: address the measured divergence for sufficient contrast and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: All tested templates have zero main/navigation landmarks and no h1; Lighthouse fails landmark-one-main. Keyboard focus remains visible, but page structure is not logical for assistive technology.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance accessibility: address the measured divergence for structure and focus and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: Narrow screenshots reflow without horizontal overflow, but Lighthouse target-size fails and many interactive links measure only 14 to 15px high. No essential media requiring captions appears in the audited paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance accessibility: address the measured divergence for zoom reflow targets and media and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: Direct probes confirm standards mode and an HTML doctype, but image audit reports 17/17 missing dimensions, 16 legacy formats, and one oversized asset.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance html: address the measured divergence for sound document and assets and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: The page uses the platform cleanly: no deprecated APIs, no avoidable BFCache blockers, no broken source maps or inspector issues, no stale vulnerable libraries, no paste-prevention on inputs, and no notification/geolocation prompts on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports five BFCache failure reasons and missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript on all tested templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance html: address the measured divergence for browser platform hygiene and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.evidence: Homepage and game detail have descriptive metadata, but /gamelist has an empty meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance html: address the measured divergence for title and description and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Viewport meta and robots.txt are present, but Lighthouse finds non-crawlable anchors on /gamelist and the DOM contains many href="#" pseudo-links with generic or empty text.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance html: address the measured divergence for crawlable and mobile friendly and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Public pages expose the indexing signals search engines need: successful HTTP status, canonical URL when appropriate, hreflang for localized variants, robots/sitemap consistency, and no accidental noindex/noarchive policy.

findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance html: address the measured divergence for canonical and indexing signals and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.evidence: Game detail has accurate Open Graph metadata but no JSON-LD for the visible game entity; homepage also has no structured data.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance html: address the measured divergence for structured and shareable metadata and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; analytics cookies use SameSite=None and two are not Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance security: address the measured divergence for secure transport and headers and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found nine third-party origins and active Google Tag Manager/DoubleClick; HAR records analytics and consent SDK traffic on first load.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance privacy: address the measured divergence for data minimisation and third parties and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Permission prompts are requested in context (not on load), and authentication uses modern, phishing-resistant methods (passkeys / WebAuthn) where relevant rather than passwords alone.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt fired on load, but the public signup offers email/social identity only and no passkey/WebAuthn path was exposed. The scanned Google API key is treated as a likely public client key, not a secret.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance passkeys: address the measured divergence for in context permissions and modern auth and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: HSTS, X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors are set, but Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are missing and CSP retains unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance security: address the measured divergence for defensive browser policies and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: The page has lang=en, dir=ltr and hreflang links for many locales, but loaded CSS inspection found 22 physical left/right rules and zero logical-property rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance translator: address the measured divergence for lang dir and logical properties and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Forms prevent and recover from mistakes humanely: validate after interaction (not prematurely), give clear required-field feedback, announce errors accessibly, and signal invalid fields visibly rather than blaming the user.
findings.evidence: Signup email fields have no associated labels or required semantics; clicking Create an account with an empty field produced no visible, accessible inline recovery message in the captured state.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance accessible-error-announcement: address the measured divergence for humane error handling and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: Image audit reports 16 legacy-format images, 8 without responsive sources, 16 below-fold images without lazy loading, and one oversized logo.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance deliver-optimized-decorative-images: address the measured divergence for optimised assets and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: The landing page transfers 4.99MB and opens analytics, consent, Sentry and realtime/legacy runtime scripts before the user interacts; script transfer alone is 3.88MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance deprioritize-background-fetches: address the measured divergence for no wasteful work and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes nearly all 4.99MB to non-main origins and tracker evidence finds nine third-party origins; Google tag scripts alone transfer about 324KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance efficient-background-processing: address the measured divergence for third party and media budget and verify under the same captured conditions.

findings.summary: Heap size and DOM node count are reasonable for what the page is; the footprint is proportionate rather than bloated.
findings.evidence: The gamelist baseline heap contains about 950,016 nodes and 64.0MB self-size before interaction, disproportionate for a public catalogue view and consistent with its multi-megabyte runtime.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply Modern Web Guidance defer-rendering-heavy-content: address the measured divergence for bounded footprint and verify under the same captured conditions.
